stem.en: A heavy box is dragged across a rough floor at a steady speed. Which statement about the work done against friction is correct?

text.en: It is stored in the box, and the box will move back when it is let go.
It is stored in the box as potential energy, because the box was pushed.
It is stored in the floor, because the floor is scratched as the box moves.
It is not stored: it goes into heat and sound in the box and the floor.

explanation.en: Work done against friction is not stored. Nothing pulls the box back, so it will not move back by itself. The energy goes into heat and sound: the box and the floor get a little warmer. Potential energy is stored only when the shape of an object changes, or when objects that attract or repel each other change position.

hints.en: Let go of the box. Does anything make it move back?
Rub your hands together hard. Where does the work go?
